item.title: Grace Wilson Gives Ophelia a Second Act in 'Gia Ophelia' – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: Grace Wilson is an emerging writer and student of NIDA’s Master of Fine Arts Dramatic Writing course whose one-woman play, 'Gia Ophelia', is getting a new run at KXT on Broadway.

item.title: Tim Dashwood: Fighting For The Stage – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: Ahead of his upcoming masterclass Fighting For The Stage, we caught up with NIDA educator Tim Dashwood to get his insights into the craft of stage combat and physical storytelling.

item.title: Grace McCann's Message to NIDA Students – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: At the start of the academic year, NIDA alum Grace McCann (Props & Effects, 2024), delivered an inspiring address to students, reflecting on her first year in the industry.

item.title: Tropfest: Roughcut is coming to NIDA – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: Hosted at NIDA and bringing together emerging filmmakers, industry voices and creative leaders for honest conversations, practical learning and meaningful connection, Tropfest: Roughcut is for emerging and early-career filmmakers who want to take their ideas further.

item.title: NIDA's 2026 Festival of Emerging Artists – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: The Festival of Emerging Artists showcases the major projects of NIDA’s Master of Fine Arts (MFA) Directing course, with the soon to be graduating directors each presenting a 40-minute stage production from March 25-28, free to the public.

item.title: NIDA Hosts the 58th Australian Writers’ Guild Awards – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: Theatre practitioners from across the state have been recognised at this year's Sydney Theatre Awards held at the Seymour Centre on 20 January. Hosted by Marney McQueen (Acting, 2003), the ceremony celebrated excellence across both mainstage and independent theatre productions, with alumni securing wins across multiple categories including directing, design, and performance. Congratulations to everyone nominated and the winning productions

item.title: Where to Watch NIDA Alumni in March 2026 – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: Find out where to watch NIDA alumni this March.

item.title: NIDA's 2026 Major Scholarships Welcome Reception – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: On Tuesday 24 February NIDA held its annual Major Scholarships Welcome Reception to welcome 28 incoming students who received Major scholarships for 2026, and thank our donors, corporate partners, trusts and foundations for their vital support which have made these scholarships possible.

item.title: Minerva Khodabande's Extraordinary Range – The National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA)
item.description: NIDA alum Minerva Khodabande (Acting, 2025) is demonstrating her range, starring in two strikingly different productions that showcase some of the most exciting storytelling currently on Sydney’s stages.
